text:
St. Louis arrives at New Jersey on the third game of a four-game road trip, 2-3-0 in its last five and coming off a 3-1 loss at the Rangers, a team that had gone four games without a win. The Blues are playing without Dillon Dube. The Devils have won four of five, the latest a 4-3 shootout win over Edmonton that ended the Oilers' three-game winning streak. They are better than their record: we count 59 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in their games, and goaltending has cost them.

The gap shows up in how the teams create and prevent chances. New Jersey generates 3.42 expected goals per 60 minutes and allows 2.41, while St. Louis sits at 3.03 and 3.06. The Devils also hold the edge on the power play (0.78 expected goals per game to 0.51) and the penalty kill (0.45 allowed to 0.52). In net, Joel Hofer is projected for the Blues at 5.1 goals saved above expected this season, which measures how many more goals he has stopped than an average goalie would on the same shots. Connor Hellebuyck, projected for the Devils, is at -0.5 over three games, though he was +3.4 across 57 starts last season. Our model has the Devils at 3.16 expected goals tonight and the Blues at 2.69.

Jack Hughes leads the watch list at 39 percent to score, and Nico Hischier is two points from 500 for his career. Arseny Gritsyuk has 10 points in his last ten games, and Mike Fink of The Hockey News posted that he "with the goal in shootout to win it." For St. Louis, Mason McTavish has gone pointless in five straight despite 3.4 expected goals, and Pius Suter is one goal from 100.
